_note: B-44. Risky-user, user-fact and device-fact read levers on the mock tenant (fixtures/tenant/<client>/risky-users.json and the base tenant file). Mock only; no real Entra Identity Protection is called. Reading real risky users needs Entra ID P2, which is UNVERIFIED per client.

levers.name: risk.list-users
levers.description: Read the client's risky users (risk level, state, detail) from the mock of Entra Identity Protection riskyUsers. Needs Entra ID P2, UNVERIFIED per client; a client without data gets an empty list and a note. Technician view only.

level.description: Only users at this risk level (default all)

impact.L1: A technician sees which of one client's people the sign-in risk engine flags; nothing about them changes, but who is flagged is personal data.
impact.L2: The client's risky-user list is read only by staff scoped to that client, so a possible account takeover is noticed before it spreads.
impact.L3: Every read is registered, scoped and audited by who asked; the results themselves are not copied into the audit.
impact.L4: Risk lists never mix across tenants, and the P2 dependency is stated per client, so an empty list is never read as all clear.

levers.name: risk.user-facts
levers.description: Read one user's directory facts (name, title, enabled, kinds of sign-in methods) for the client. Mock of Graph user; phone numbers are not returned. Technician view only.

upn.description: userPrincipalName of one user of this client

impact.L1: A technician sees one person's job title, whether the account is on, and which kinds of sign-in method they have; nothing changes.
impact.L2: The analyst sees the person behind an alert in one place, scoped to the client the alert came from.
impact.L3: Each read is registered, scoped and audited by who asked about whom; the facts are not copied into the audit.
impact.L4: Directory facts never cross clients, and contact numbers stay out of the result.

levers.name: risk.device-facts
levers.description: Read the devices on record for one user of the client (name, OS, managed, compliance, last check-in). Stand-in device list; field names UNVERIFIED. Technician view only.

upn.description: userPrincipalName of one user of this client

impact.L1: A technician sees which devices belong to one person and whether they are managed and compliant; nothing changes.
impact.L2: The analyst can tell an unmanaged phone from a company laptop when judging an alert.
impact.L3: Each read is registered, scoped and audited by who asked about whom; the device list is not copied into the audit.
impact.L4: Device lists are picked by the client's own id, so one office's devices never appear in another's pack.
